faq.q: How does an AND gate work?
faq.a: An AND gate gives an output of 1 only if both inputs are 1. Built from switches, it is two switches in series: the lamp lights only when both are closed.

faq.q: How does an OR gate work?
faq.a: An OR gate gives 1 if either input, or both, is 1. Built from switches, it is two switches in parallel: closing either one gives the current a path to the lamp.
A NOT gate flips its input: 1 becomes 0 and 0 becomes 1. In a transistor circuit, a high input turns the transistor on, which pulls the output low.
asks: How do you make a NOT gate?

faq.q: Why do computers use transistors instead of switches?
faq.a: Transistors are switches with no moving parts, worked by electricity. They can be made billions of times smaller than a finger and switch billions of times a second.
asks: Are logic gates made of transistors?

faq.q: What do 1 and 0 mean in a logic gate?
faq.a: They stand for two voltage levels: 1 is on, a higher voltage, and 0 is off, close to zero volts. Using just two levels keeps circuits reliable even with a little electrical noise.
asks: What is binary in a circuit?

facts: Claude Shannon showed in 1937 that circuits of switches can carry out Boolean logic.
George Boole described the algebra of true and false that logic gates follow in 1854.

quiz.say: Two switches are in series with a lamp. When does the lamp light?
quiz.show: Two switches are in series with a lamp. When does the lamp light?

options.show: Only when both switches are closed
options.say: Only when both switches are closed

quiz.why: In series there is one path, so both switches must be closed: that is AND.

wrong.1: That describes switches in parallel, an OR gate.
wrong.2: With both open there is no path at all.
